title: High-throughput Point-Cloud Accelerator with Sparsity-aware Hierarchical Neighbor Voxel Search and Skipping
problem: 3D sparse convolution networks for point cloud processing face challenges from irregular voxel sparsity patterns, increasing hardware complexity and reducing efficiency when exploiting sparsity.
motivation: Point cloud processing is increasingly used in 3D vision applications, but irregular sparsity patterns make it difficult for traditional accelerators to achieve high utilization and throughput.
method: The approach combines algorithm and hardware design to handle sparse point clouds efficiently. The algorithm skips empty voxels (tiny 3D boxes that partition the point cloud) based on a threshold. The hardware uses a 3-stage hierarchical search engine that progressively narrows which voxels contain data, adapting to the irregular sparsity patterns of each point cloud. This eliminates wasted computation by processing only the voxels with actual data.
key_novelty: A hierarchical multi-stage search pipeline that progressively narrows which voxels to process based on sparsity patterns, combined with threshold-based skipping made during processing to eliminate wasted work.
contributions: On-the-fly threshold-based voxel skipping algorithm to enhance efficiency
Hierarchical 3-stage Voxel Search and Skipping hardware engine to systematically reduce search space
77.7% reduction in delay compared to baseline without sparsity adaptations
1.34x higher energy efficiency and 2.22x higher throughput vs state-of-the-art in 65nm process
limitations: Paper does not discuss scalability to larger point clouds, memory bandwidth requirements, or comparison with dense convolution approaches.
primary_theme: Hierarchical sparsity-aware point cloud 3D convolution accelerator
